purpose: One universal mathematical word law across music, SDR, astronomy, FPGA clock ratios and phonemic metrical patterns; no device driver or D2 language control.

source.name: Author SENS radio channel laboratory
source.claim: Frequency offset, sample-rate scaling, aligned bit timing are observed in real SENS radio tests; this does NOT prove a new universal opcode.

source.name: Author Spanda exact p/q analog FPGA vision
source.claim: Exact rational clock and oscillator design supports discrete p/q word pacing; design intent is not actual SENS runtime parity.

candidates.signature: (positive_integer_period_n, event_count_k_in_[0,n], rational_phase_rho_in_[0,1)) -> finite D1 bit sequence length n
candidates.law: For i=0..n−1 output D1 bit floor((i+1)*k/n + rho)-floor(i*k/n + rho). No floating-point approximation, no implicit hardware clock, and no two-valued T5 code.
invariants: For every prefix of length m, number of ones is floor(m*k/n+rho)-floor(rho)
For every contiguous pair of subwords of equal length, one-count discrepancy is at most one (balanced)
Every full period repeats; periodic output is not a physical timing guarantee
falsifiers: An 8-step, 3-event output with adjacent long clumps (e.g. 11100000) breaks balanced prefix behavior
An off-by-one period that returns k−1 or k+1 events is incorrect
A floating accumulator whose rounding changes the binary word at exact rational ties violates identity
A rotation of a word may be a useful musical variant but does not in general satisfy the same rho=0 identity
candidates.possible_library_derivation: Can be built from integer floor, exact rationals and sequence iteration; derived does not imply excluded, but primitive importance needs explicit owner finding.
candidates.independent_root_challenge: Determine if a separately named universal binary word has an observable contract and cross-substrate benefit beyond existing exact arithmetic and fold. Exact-name absence is only prefilter.
target_interfaces: text prosody/meter as abstract binary weight pattern
